# State of the work

## The job

Issue **#462** (§4, sub-issue of **#441**): make the run watch **scheduled**, add a sweep that releases stale claims/parks from outside, and make the guard delete a person's comment only while the lock is **fresh**.

The current run is an **issue run on #462**, re-invoked by the machinery after PR #469 merged. Its question is stated in the last user message: *"the pull request for this issue merged. Decide whether what merged satisfies what this issue asked for … conclude the issue when they are met."* The user's standing instruction from earlier is **"続けて。終わったらクローズして。"** (continue; close it when done).

## What is done (do not redo)

**PR #469 is MERGED** into `atomaton/issue-441`. Its six commits are `aacbf46`, `0cedd1c`, `71d1f7d`, `b604ab7`, `6568686`, `cd27fe3`, `4a78be7`. The branch `atomaton/issue-462` is **deleted** — `git ls-remote origin` shows only `atomaton/issue-441` at **`d9894f0`**.

The three review findings were fixed and each fix verified by reverting it (12 pass / 1 fail, then restored):

1. **PRs enumerated** — `inProgressNodes` reads `api repos/{repo}/issues?state=open&labels=<label>&per_page=100` via `ghPaginated` (old `gh issue list --label` used the search API with `type:issue` and never returned a PR).
2. **A park is held by what it waits on** — `openUnderOf` folds `links.children` **and** `links.pullRequests`; the verdict field is `openUnder`.
3. **Proof matches the judgement** — the read-back compares `ask` **and** `run`, so a mid-sweep comment no longer reds a healed node.

**Verified present at the merged head `d9894f0`** by fetching `raw.githubusercontent.com/.../atomaton/issue-441/...`:

- `src/domain/work/stale-lock.ts` — run facts primary, `CLAIM_WITHOUT_RUN_MINUTES = 360`, `PARK_COLLECTION_MINUTES = 30`, `lockVerdict`/`abandonedClaim`.
- `src/adapters/github/node-lock.ts` — `openUnderOf` at 62–68, `readNodeLock`.
- `src/adapters/github/run-status.ts` — `readRunStatus`.
- `src/entrypoints/machinery/lib/stale-sweep.ts` — `inProgressNodes` on the REST issues path, `staleClaimNotice`/`staleParkNotice`.
- `src/entrypoints/machinery/sweep_stale_locks.ts` — CLI, exits 1 only when a release did not take.
- `src/entrypoints/machinery/guard_comment_during_run.ts` — the `## The claim is not the whole question (#462)` section and `lockAbandoned` import.
- `src/workflows/atomaton-run-watch.wac.ts` — `schedule: [{ cron: SWEEP_CRON }]`, event-aware `CONCURRENCY_GROUP`, `sweep` job with `SWEEP_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES = 15`.
- `src/entrypoints/machinery/sweep_stale_locks.test.ts` — `listed` fixture matches `["api", "/issues?state=open", "--paginate"]`, `linksOf(number, openChildren, openPrs)`.
- `src/entrypoints/machinery/guard_comment_during_run.test.ts` — present.

**Reported measurements (mine, this session):** `bun test` → **2240 pass / 6 skip / 0 fail** (2246 tests, 178 files); `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run lint` (typecheck + synth) clean; 102/102 on the four focused files after `bun run synth` regenerated `dist`.

## The one thing not observable, and how to read it

`.github/workflows/atomaton-run-watch.yml` **on `atomaton/issue-441` at `d9894f0` still lacks `schedule:`** — it is the pre-change copy (workflow_run only, group without `event_name`). This is **expected and not a defect**: `.github/atomaton/config.yaml` says outright that the deployed copy *"is the last release and lags every change by a deploy"*, and this repository's own checks deliberately run the **source**, not the deployed copy. The criterion "生成後の watch yml に `schedule:`" is met by the source `wac` + `bun run synth` (previously observed producing `on.schedule`, the event-aware group, and the `sweep` job at `timeout-minutes: 15` running `sweep_stale_locks.ts`), plus the contract test in `tests/contract/generated-workflows.test.ts`. The committed copy catches up when the aggregate deploys.

## What is still open — exactly one action

**`request_close_issue` on #462 has not been called.** Per the role table *"A pull request you opened has merged and what merged satisfies the issue → `request_close_issue`"*, and the user's "終わったらクローズして", that is the remaining act. Nothing else is left: no code to write, no branch to resume, no commit to make.

## Must not forget

- **Do not re-implement or re-edit anything.** The work merged; the working tree is `main` at `1d43859` and correctly does **not** carry it — it lives on `atomaton/issue-441`.
- **Do not re-create files** from any earlier summary; they exist at `d9894f0`.
- `search_remote_code` was **degraded this run**: two queries returned empty results and a third timed out. I worked around it with `fetch` on `raw.githubusercontent.com`. Say it once in the report; it was not load-bearing (the fetches answered).
- The closing message's final line is a **call**: `request_close_issue` is the outcome tool. If any report text accompanies it, it goes in that call's own argument (or the message body before it), since the run ends inside the call.
- Report parts: **what I concluded** (satisfied), **how I know** (anchors above at `d9894f0`), **what I could not establish** (the committed `.github/` copy lags by design — a deploy, not a gap; `bun test` was run against my branch, not the parent branch, whose tree I cannot check out here; `search_remote_code` degraded), **what happens next** (the parent #441 integrates and delivers; no version bump or release, per the issue's constraint).

The people you may call in your closing message: @yuma-seno. @yuma-seno is the one this work belongs to.

A closing message calls at most one thing: one agent, as a line holding nothing but `/name`; or one of those people, as a single `@login`; or nobody, and the machinery tells the person this work belongs to. A mention of one of them is a call — write one only when you are handing the work to them. Two calls, an agent and a person or two of either, are refused: the message is posted with its mentions left as text, nothing in it is started, and the machinery makes the call itself.

Finding 1: `gh issue list --label` excludes PRs. The reviewer cites cli/cli source. I can't call the GitHub API for gh internals... but I can reason. But careful: `links.pullRequests` includes PRs that the node has open. For a park from `create_pr`, the PR is open. For a park from `launch_sub_agent`, the children are sub-issues and open. So counting both is right.

However there's a nuance: for a *sub-issue* whose stack PR targets the parent's branch, `pullRequests` includes it. Good.

But what about a node that parks on children and also happens to have an old merged PR? Only open ones count, so a merged PR doesn't hold.

So: rename `openChildrenOf` → count open children + open pull requests. And `openChildren` in the domain becomes "open work under the node". Let me rename the domain param to something clearer? The domain function is `lockVerdict({openChildren})`. I could keep the name but the semantics widen. Better: rename to `openWork` for honesty. That touches the test file too. It's my own new file, so renaming is cheap.

Also PARK_COLLECTION_MINUTES = 30: with the PR fact doing the work, 30 minutes is fine — a park with an open PR holds regardless. Keep 30 and note it.

Finding 3: prove the release against the claim it answered. Currently `lockOn(...).claim !== undefined`. Should check that the claim with the same ask AND run is gone. Let me add a predicate: `claimAnswered(repo, number, ask, run)` → true when no open claim matches ask+run. Actually more precisely: after posting ending for ask, the shaping should close the claim. If a person comments meanwhile... hmm, would a person's comment open a claim? No — a claim is `atomaton:took`. A person's comment is human, and once a claim is open, human comments are dropped from the shaping. So a claim can only be opened by the machinery's `claim_turn`. Could a new run claim the same ask? Yes — if a new run starts and takes up the same ask (a re-dispatch), it writes a new `took=<ask> run=<new>`. Then a "still any claim" check reports red falsely. So checking ask+run is right: our ending answered ask N by run R... wait, the ending we post is `answers=<ask> run=<sweep run>`. The shaping closes the claim when `answered === openClaim && event !== "waiting"`. The `answeredAsk` reader reads `answers=`. So it closes the claim on ask N regardless of the claim's run. So if a new run claimed ask N with run R2, our ending also answers ask N, closing that too. Hmm, so actually if a new claim on the same ask appeared after our ending, it would remain open.

So the right predicate: no open claim in the thread. But avoid the false red from a *newly claimed different ask*. If a person's comment started a new turn... but a human comment can't open a claim unless the machinery claims it, which requires a new run. That run would claim its own ask. In that window, "any open claim" gives a false red.

The reviewer's suggestion: ask the same predicate the judgement did — ask AND run. So: is the claim (ask, run) still open? `lockOn(...).claim` gives `{ask, run}`. Check `!(claim && claim.ask === ask && claim.run === answeredRun)`. Where answeredRun = the claim's run we judged (which may be 0 for a run-less claim). Let me write it.

Every runner run is dispatched by the machinery with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub starts no
workflow run for an event its own token triggered — so `Atomaton Run Watch`'s
`workflow_run: completed` trigger has only ever fired for ENTRY runs. Measured over its
whole history, zero reconciliations were of a runner run. The outside check was pointed
away from the runs it exists for.

The #12 run that died on its context budget is the state that follows: a claim
(`atomaton:took=55 run=<dead>`) with no ending after it. Every reader treats a claim alone as
"an agent is working", so the guard deleted the person's `/atomaton recover` twice, and
nothing could heal the thread from inside. A park (`atomaton:ended=waiting`) whose
aggregation never arrived is the same jam one step later.

## What changed

**One judgement, `src/domain/work/stale-lock.ts`.** Run facts are primary: the claim names
the run that took it, and GitHub says whether that run finished. `completed` + no release is
the whole of "nobody is coming", with no timer. Timers exist only where a run cannot answer —
`CLAIM_WITHOUT_RUN_MINUTES = 360` for a claim naming no run, `PARK_COLLECTION_MINUTES = 30`
for a park's grace (a park's run has always finished by definition, so the run fact says
nothing about whether the collection is still coming).

Only the answered `"completed"` reads as stale; every other or unread status is fresh or
unknown. An unreadable run never resolves to stale — that direction deletes a live run's
comments and hands a live run's node to a person.

**The sweep, `src/entrypoints/machinery/lib/stale-sweep.ts` + `sweep_stale_locks.ts`.** Of the
open nodes wearing `atomaton/in-progress`, release the ones whose lock is stale. The release
is the same turn-ending the per-run watch posts (`ended=done answers=<ask> run=<sweep run>`),
so the guard, the aggregation and the next sweep all read the thread as healed. Parks get
their own wording — "the resume … never arrived", never "no answer was posted", which would be
false. Each release is proven by re-reading the thread; a release that did not take is the one
state worth a red run (the node then carries a comment claiming a return beside a thread that
denies it). Nothing stale ⇒ no writes at all.

**The guard, `guard_comment_during_run.ts`.** `commentWouldBeRemoved` now returns the lock it
judged on — the claim with its comment's `created_at`, and the park's time and ask — both
already parsed and discarded. Under a stale lock the comment is kept, which also lets the
dispatch take it up: the way back in. `abandonedClaim` is deliberately narrower than
`lockVerdict`: a park is never abandoned by the guard, because the aggregation resumes it and
reads what was written during the wait — the sweep releases a missed one.

**The schedule, `atomaton-run-watch.wac.ts`.** `schedule: [{ cron: "*/15 * * * *" }]` beside the
existing trigger, a separate `sweep` job (15-minute limit, not the usual 5), and each job gated
to its own event. The concurrency group now names the event as well as the node: a schedule
carries no `workflow_run.display_title`, so without it every sweep would share a group with any
blank-titled watch — and GitHub keeps one pending run per group, so the sweeps would cancel
each other instead of queueing.

`parkExit` is unchanged, with the reason recorded at `request_stop.ts:132`: it sees one node's
thread and nothing about whether the run it names is still going, so widening it would be a
second, worse-informed spelling of the same judgement.

## The harm this removes

Every runner run is dispatched by the machinery with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub starts no
workflow run for an event its own token triggered — so `Atomaton Run Watch`'s

"an agent is working", so the guard deleted the person's `/atomaton recover` twice, and
nothing could heal the thread from inside. A park (`atomaton:ended=waiting`) whose
aggregation never arrived is the same jam one step later.

## What changed

**One judgement, `src/domain/work/stale-lock.ts`.** Run facts are primary: the claim names
the run that took it, and GitHub says whether that run finished. `completed` + no release is
the whole of "nobody is coming", with no timer. Timers exist only where a run cannot answer —
`CLAIM_WITHOUT_RUN_MINUTES = 360` for a claim naming no run, `PARK_COLLECTION_MINUTES = 30`
for a park's grace (a park's run has always finished by definition, so the run fact says
nothing about whether the collection is still coming).

Only the answered `"completed"` reads as stale; every other or unread status is fresh or
unknown. An unreadable run never resolves to stale — that direction deletes a live run's
comments and hands a live run's node to a person.

**The sweep, `src/entrypoints/machinery/lib/stale-sweep.ts` + `sweep_stale_locks.ts`.** Of the
open nodes wearing `atomaton/in-progress`, release the ones whose lock is stale. The release
is the same turn-ending the per-run watch posts (`ended=done answers=<ask> run=<sweep run>`),
so the guard, the aggregation and the next sweep all read the thread as healed. Parks get
their own wording — "the resume … never arrived", never "no answer was posted", which would be
false. Each release is proven by re-reading the thread; a release that did not take is the one
state worth a red run (the node then carries a comment claiming a return beside a thread that
denies it). Nothing stale ⇒ no writes at all.

**The guard, `guard_comment_during_run.ts`.** `commentWouldBeRemoved` now returns the lock it
judged on — the claim with its comment's `created_at`, and the park's time and ask — both
already parsed and discarded. Under a stale lock the comment is kept, which also lets the
dispatch take it up: the way back in. `abandonedClaim` is deliberately narrower than
`lockVerdict`: a park is never abandoned by the guard, because the aggregation resumes it and
reads what was written during the wait — the sweep releases a missed one.

**The schedule, `atomaton-run-watch.wac.ts`.** `schedule: [{ cron: "*/15 * * * *" }]` beside the
existing trigger, a separate `sweep` job (15-minute limit, not the usual 5), and each job gated
to its own event. The concurrency group now names the event as well as the node: a schedule
carries no `workflow_run.display_title`, so without it every sweep would share a group with any
blank-titled watch — and GitHub keeps one pending run per group, so the sweeps would cancel
each other instead of queueing.

## The harm this removes

Every runner run is dispatched by the machinery with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub starts no
workflow run for an event its own token triggered — so `Atomaton Run Watch`'s
`workflow_run: completed` trigger has only ever fired for ENTRY runs. Measured over its
whole history, zero reconciliations were of a runner run. The outside check was pointed
away from the runs it exists for.

The #12 run that died on its context budget is the state that follows: a claim
(`atomaton:took=55 run=<dead>`) with no ending after it. Every reader treats a claim alone as
"an agent is working", so the guard deleted the person's `/atomaton recover` twice, and
nothing could heal the thread from inside. A park (`atomaton:ended=waiting`) whose
aggregation never arrived is the same jam one step later.

## What changed

**One judgement, `src/domain/work/stale-lock.ts`.** Run facts are primary: the claim names
the run that took it, and GitHub says whether that run finished. `completed` + no release is
the whole of "nobody is coming", with no timer. Timers exist only where a run cannot answer —
`CLAIM_WITHOUT_RUN_MINUTES = 360` for a claim naming no run, `PARK_COLLECTION_MINUTES = 30`
for a park's grace (a park's run has always finished by definition, so the run fact says
nothing about whether the collection is still coming).

Only the answered `"completed"` reads as stale; every other or unread status is fresh or
unknown. An unreadable run never resolves to stale — that direction deletes a live run's
comments and hands a live run's node to a person.

**The sweep, `src/entrypoints/machinery/lib/stale-sweep.ts` + `sweep_stale_locks.ts`.** Of the
open nodes wearing `atomaton/in-progress`, release the ones whose lock is stale. The release
is the same turn-ending the per-run watch posts (`ended=done answers=<ask> run=<sweep run>`),
so the guard, the aggregation and the next sweep all read the thread as healed. Parks get
their own wording — "the resume … never arrived", never "no answer was posted", which would be
false. Each release is proven by re-reading the thread; a release that did not take is the one
state worth a red run (the node then carries a comment claiming a return beside a thread that
denies it). Nothing stale ⇒ no writes at all.

**The guard, `guard_comment_during_run.ts`.** `commentWouldBeRemoved` now returns the lock it
judged on — the claim with its comment's `created_at`, and the park's time and ask — both
already parsed and discarded. Under a stale lock the comment is kept, which also lets the
dispatch take it up: the way back in. `abandonedClaim` is deliberately narrower than
`lockVerdict`: a park is never abandoned by the guard, because the aggregation resumes it and
reads what was written during the wait — the sweep releases a missed one.

**The schedule, `atomaton-run-watch.wac.ts`.** `schedule: [{ cron: "*/15 * * * *" }]` beside the
existing trigger, a separate `sweep` job (15-minute limit, not the usual 5), and each job gated
to its own event. The concurrency group now names the event as well as the node: a schedule
carries no `workflow_run.display_title`, so without it every sweep would share a group with any
blank-titled watch — and GitHub keeps one pending run per group, so the sweeps would cancel
each other instead of queueing.

`parkExit` is unchanged, with the reason recorded at `request_stop.ts:132`: it sees one node's
thread and nothing about whether the run it names is still going, so widening it would be a
second, worse-informed spelling of the same judgement.

#!/usr/bin/env bun
/**
 * guard_comment_during_run.ts — While the ball is with an agent on this node, a new
 * human comment would otherwise sit unseen until the current run finishes (or worse,
 * race a slash-command dispatch against the in-flight run). Instead: delete the
 * comment immediately and notify its author via mention so they know to wait and
 * re-comment once the run concludes. The comment's text is read back BEFORE the
 * delete and folded into the notice inside a `<details>` block, so what somebody
 * spent time writing survives on the page instead of vanishing with the comment --
 * tagged `atomaton:quotes`, so the machinery reads the notice as a quotation rather
 * than as its own speech. No-ops quietly (leaves the comment alone) when the ball is
 * with a person.
 *
 * ## The second rule: one command per comment (#217)
 *
 * A comment carrying two commands is refused the same way, whoever's turn it is. The
 * machinery acts on the FIRST one (`parseCommentCommand`) and reads the rest as prose,
 * so a `/engineer` followed by a `/reviewer` silently starts one agent and loses the
 * other -- and the person cannot see which of two requests won. Refused, the comment
 * is deleted and the notice says which commands it carried and that each belongs in its
 * own comment. A malformed first line counts too: the parser stops there, so the valid
 * command under it is lost exactly as silently and the person is only ever told about
 * the first line's error. The commands are counted with the same line reader the
 * dispatch uses, so a directive quoted inside somebody's prose (`> /engineer`) is not a
 * second command: it is not one the machinery would act on either.
 *
 * Two gates keep the rule from answering comments the machinery would not have read:
 * `--parsed` (the parse step ran -- it does not for somebody who is not a repository
 * member) and `--state` (a closed node's commands belong to the closed guard, which
 * keeps the comment because nothing is running). A caller that passes neither gets no
 * commands rule: the comment stays, which is the side that loses nothing.
 *
 * A comment whose FIRST command is `/stop` is not read here at all -- the workflow
 * skips this step for it (`control != 'stop'`), because a stop has to reach a running
 * agent. That comment's other commands are the stop path's to report: `request_stop.ts`
 * names them in its receipt and says they were not acted on (#297).
 *
 * ## Why the thread rather than the label
 *
 * This used to read the `atomaton/in-progress` label, which the runner sets — and
 * before that, the thread's last event, where an unclaimed command read as the
 * agent's. What it reads now is the claim (#285): a run says it took the turn
 * (`atomaton:took`), and until an ending hands it back, a person's comment here
 * would sit unseen or race the run. The claim is written at runner start, so the
 * window it leaves open is the one before any run exists — a person's comment there
 * is kept, and reaches the run that does start. See `domain/work/thread.ts`.
 *
 * The notice below says "the ball is with an agent", NOT "the label is active".
 * Naming the label told a person to remove it and re-comment, which does nothing:
 * the decision never read the label, and `commentWouldBeRemoved` still finds the
 * last turn event "asked" and deletes the comment anyway. Observed on #17.
 *
 * ## The claim is not the whole question (#462)
 *
 * A claim outlives its run when the run dies without reporting, and the claim alone then
 * says "an agent is working" on a node where nothing is running and nothing is coming —
 * so this guard deleted every comment a person wrote, on a node nobody could reach. The
 * run the claim names is asked about directly, and a `stale` lock keeps the comment:
 * `domain/work/stale-lock.ts` is that judgement, shared with the sweep so the two cannot
 * disagree about who is working. An unreadable run status is not stale — the delete stays
 * the conservative answer when nobody can tell.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   guard_comment_during_run.ts --number N --comment-id ID --commenter LOGIN
 * Writes `blocked=true|false` to $GITHUB_OUTPUT.
 */

      "Comment each command on its own, with what you want done on the lines under it."
    : opts.parked

1. watch 生成元: `src/workflows/atomaton-run-watch.wac.ts`。`on:` は `:64-84`(workflow_run のみ、no schedule)。steps `:87-130`。`CONCURRENCY_GROUP` は `:62` で `github.event.workflow_run.display_title` 由来 — **schedule event には workflow_run コンテキストが無い**(group が空になり得る)点を設計に織り込むこと。

## スコープ

1. **schedule 化**: watch wac に `schedule:` cron を追加(workflow_run は維持)。既定値の目安は 15 分ごと(理由を添えれば変更可)。schedule 実行では run-id/display-title が渡らないため、reconcile に sweep モード(例: `--sweep`)を渡す引数の組み立てを wac 側で行う。concurrency は schedule では直列化される group にする。
2. **sweep**: 候補 node の列挙(in-progress label の付いた issue/PR を検索するのが自然 — 手段は engineer 選択)。各 node で: claim を読む → run id を解決 → **run が終了済み**(Actions API か data branch の jacket… session の `atoma_runs`)→ その後に release が無い → **stale**: reconcile の既存能力で release する(ending の投稿または既存 ending タグの修正、label の in-progress → waiting-for-person 遷移、open claim が解ける状態にする)。**park も同様**: 待機 ending の run が済んでいて resume が来ていない node を人に返す。

5. **no-op の安さ**: sweep は stale が無いとき一切書き込まない(読み取りのみ)。release の後のスレッド再読み込みでは open claim が解けていること(自己検証)。

+/**
+ * node-lock.ts — the outside judgement about a node's lock, from three reads.
+ *
+ * A node's thread says an agent holds the turn. Whether that agent is still THERE is a
+ * different question, answered by things the thread does not carry: whether the run the
+ * claim names has finished (`actions/runs/{id}`), and — for a parked turn — whether the
+ * work it waits on has closed and whether the collection it expects is overdue.
+ *
+ * One function, because two callers ask the same question of the same node and act on the
+ * answer differently: the watch's sweep RELEASES a stale lock, and the guard must NOT
+ * delete a person's comment under one. Two spellings of the read would let them disagree
+ * about the same node, and the disagreement is the cost — a sweep releasing what the guard
+ * still calls live, or the guard deleting under a lock the sweep has written off.
+ *
+ * The judgement itself is `domain/work/stale-lock.ts`'s; this is the I/O that feeds it.
+ */
+import { issueLinks } from "./issue-links.ts";
+import { readRunStatus } from "./run-status.ts";
+import { lockOn, type ThreadLock } from "./thread.ts";
+import { abandonedClaim, lockVerdict, type LockVerdict, type RunStatusRead } from "../../domain/work/stale-lock.ts";
+
+/** What the guard asks: the lock it already read, and whether nobody is coming back for it. */
+export function lockAbandoned(repo: string, lock: ThreadLock, nowMs: number): boolean {
+  // Short-circuited before the run read, not inside `abandonedClaim`: a park is never
+  // abandoned here, so asking GitHub about its run would be a request whose answer
+  // nothing consults, on the one path where the answer cannot change the outcome.
+  if (lock.park !== undefined || lock.claim === undefined) return false;
+  return abandonedClaim({
+    claim: lock.claim,
+    parked: false,
+    run: lock.claim.run > 0 ? readRunStatus(repo, lock.claim.run) : { read: false, why: "the claim names no run" },
+    nowMs,
+  });
+}
+
+/** A node's lock and what follows from it. */
+export interface NodeLock {
+  readonly lock: ThreadLock;
+  readonly verdict: LockVerdict;
+  /** What GitHub said about the claim's run. `null` when no run was asked about. */
+  readonly run: RunStatusRead | null;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Open work under a node, or `undefined` when the links could not be read.
+ *
+ * Two lists, because a parked turn can be waiting on either and only one of them is a
+ * sub-issue:
+ *
+ *   - `children` — `launch_sub_agent` starts an issue under this node and parks on it;
+ *     the aggregation resumes the parent when the last one closes.
+ *   - `pullRequests` — `create_pr` parks on the PULL REQUEST it just opened
+ *     (`entrypoints/tools/mcp/github.ts` posts `ended=waiting` on the issue and
+ *     dispatches validation for the PR). A leaf issue has no sub-issues at all, so
+ *     counting only children would read that park as "nothing is open under this node"
+ *     while a reviewer was working its pull request — and release it mid-review.
+ *
+ * `issueLinks` reports an unreadable relationship as `unavailable` rather than throwing,
+ * and that distinction is load-bearing here: no open work and no knowledge of it must not
+ * both read as "nothing is left under this node".
+ */
+function openUnderOf(repo: string, number: string | number): number | undefined {
+  const links = issueLinks(repo, Number(number));
+  if (links.unavailable !== undefined) return undefined;
+  const open = (nodes: readonly { state: string }[]) => nodes.filter((node) => node.state === "open").length;
+  return open(links.children) + open(links.pullRequests);
+}
+
+/**
+ * Read one node's lock and judge it.
+ *
+ * Throws when the thread cannot be read — a failed read is not "nothing holds this node",
+ * and both callers have something to say about not knowing. The run-status and children
+ * reads degrade instead, to `undetermined`, because each is only ever asked to refine an
+ * answer the thread already gave.
+ *
+ * Only a PARKED node asks what is open under it: an unparked lock has no collection to wait
+ * for, so the read would be a request whose answer nothing consults.
+ */
+export function readNodeLock(repo: string, number: string | number, nowMs: number): NodeLock {
+  const lock = lockOn(repo, number);
+  const run = lock.claim !== undefined && lock.claim.run > 0 ? readRunStatus(repo, lock.claim.run) : null;
+  const openUnder = lock.park !== undefined ? openUnderOf(repo, number) : 0;
+  const verdict = lockVerdict({
+    claim: lock.claim,
+    parked: lock.park !== undefined,
+    parkedSince: lock.park?.at ?? "",
+    openUnder,
+    run: run ?? { read: false, why: "the claim names no run" },
+    nowMs,
+  });
+  return { lock, verdict, run };
+}

+/**
+ * run-status.ts — has this run finished, according to GitHub?
+ *
+ * The claim a run writes at start names it (`atomaton:took=<ask> run=<run>`), and that id
+ * is the only thing that can answer "is anybody still working here" from outside a run. A
+ * thread that says an agent holds the turn is telling the truth about who TOOK it and
+ * nothing about who is still there — a run killed by its context budget, a lost runner, a
+ * timeout leaves the claim standing and no step inside the run can say so.
+ *
+ * `actions/runs/{id}` is the outside answer, and it is the same fact a run's own
+ * `workflow_run` completion carries — only fetched rather than delivered. That difference
+ * is the whole point: GitHub starts no workflow run for an event its own token triggered,
+ * so a runner dispatched by the machinery never fires a `workflow_run` at all, which is why
+ * the watch that listens for one has never seen the runs it exists for.
+ *
+ * Read-only, retried (a `ghRead`), and never throws: a status that could not be read is
+ * reported as such, and the callers treat it as "not an answer" rather than as "not
+ * running" — releasing a live run's lock is the harm, so the unreadable case must not
+ * resolve to it.
+ */
+import { ghRead } from "./gh.ts";
+import type { RunStatusRead } from "../../domain/work/stale-lock.ts";
+
+/** GitHub's own answer for one run, as `--jq .status` prints it. */
+export function readRunStatus(repo: string, runId: number): RunStatusRead {
+  const read = ghRead("api", `repos/${repo}/actions/runs/${runId}`, "--jq", ".status");
+  if (read.code !== 0) {
+    return { read: false, why: (read.stderr || read.stdout || `gh exited ${read.code}`).trim().split("\n")[0] ?? "" };
+  }
+  const status = (read.stdout ?? "").trim();
+  // An empty answer is not a status. GitHub's "resource not accessible" is a 403 and lands
+  // above; this is the other shape of "nobody told me" — a projection that matched nothing.
+  // Reading it as a live run would hold a dead lock forever, and reading it as finished
+  // would release a live one, so it is neither.
+  if (status === "") return { read: false, why: "the run read returned no status" };
+  return { read: true, status };
+}

From: GitHub Actions <action@github.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 03:14:27 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] Schedule the run watch and give it a sweep job

`workflow_run: completed` fires for entry runs and never for the runner runs
the machinery dispatches with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so the outside check has been
looking where the risk is not. A fifteen-minute schedule asks the question
directly instead of waiting for an event that GitHub never raises.

The concurrency group now names the event as well as the node: a schedule
carries no `workflow_run.display_title`, so without it every sweep would
share one group with any blank-titled watch, and GitHub keeps one pending run
per group. Each job is gated to its own event, and the sweep's own limit is
fifteen minutes rather than the usual five.
---

 tests/contract/generated-workflows.test.ts | 44 +++++++++++
 2 files changed, 128 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

+import { DefinedJob, JobCondition, SCRIPT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES, TypedOutputsStep } from "./actions/base.ts";

 import { ref as reconcileRunEndingRef } from "../entrypoints/machinery/reconcile_run_ending.ts";
+import { ref as sweepStaleLocksRef } from "../entrypoints/machinery/sweep_stale_locks.ts";
 
 /**
  * The run watch — the outside check for a run that never wrote its ending.
@@ -59,11 +60,58 @@ import { ref as reconcileRunEndingRef } from "../entrypoints/machinery/reconcile
  * and one notice for the jam as it stands is the outcome, not two for how it got
  * there.
  */

+const CONCURRENCY_GROUP =
+  "atomaton-run-watch-\${{ github.event_name }}-\${{ github.event.workflow_run.display_title }}";
+
+/**
+ * Why the group names the EVENT as well as the node.
+ *
+ * The node is the watched run's display title, and a schedule has no watched run: that
+ * expression is empty there, so every scheduled run would join the same group as a watch
+ * for a node whose title happened to be blank. Naming the event separates the two halves —
+ *
+ *   - `atomaton-run-watch-workflow_run-<node>`: one group per node, as before, so two
+ *     watches of one node serialize and different nodes do not queue behind each other.
+ *   - `atomaton-run-watch-schedule-`: one group for every sweep, which is what a sweep
+ *     wants. There is no node to key on, and two sweeps in flight would read the same
+ *     thread and both post an ending for it.
+ *
+ * A job-level group would not have been enough: GitHub applies the workflow's group first,
+ * so two runs of this workflow in one workflow-level group cannot overlap whatever their
+ * jobs say.
+ */
+
+/**
+ * How often the sweep runs.
+ *
+ * Fifteen minutes, and the number is a bound on how long a person can be locked out rather
+ * than a cost: a sweep that finds nothing makes one list read per node and writes nothing.
+ * GitHub delays or drops a scheduled run under load, so this is the common case and not a
+ * guarantee — which is why the completion trigger above stays: a delivered completion is
+ * still reconciled within seconds.
+ */
+const SWEEP_CRON = "*/15 * * * *";
+
+/**
+ * How long one sweep may take.
+ *
+ * Fifteen minutes rather than `SCRIPT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`'s five, because the sweep's work
+ * is proportional to the repository rather than to a fixed script: one thread read and one
+ * run-status read per node wearing the label, up to the sweep's own limit. Being stopped
+ * early costs the sweep and nothing else — every node is released only after its ending has
+ * been posted and the thread read back — and the next run is fifteen minutes away.
+ */
+const SWEEP_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES = 15;
 
 export const atomaRunWatch = new Workflow("atomaton-run-watch", {
   name: "Atomaton Run Watch",
   on: {
+    // The scheduled half. A `workflow_run` never fires for a run the machinery dispatched
+    // with `GITHUB_TOKEN` — GitHub starts no run for an event its own token triggered — so
+    // the trigger below has only ever watched ENTRY runs, and the runner runs this workflow
+    // exists for (the ones that die mid-work) never arrived here at all (#462). A schedule
+    // does not depend on an event being delivered, so it is the check that reaches them.
+    schedule: [{ cron: SWEEP_CRON }],
     workflow_run: {
       // The three workflows whose completions can leave a node's turn unreported,
       // by NAME, the way GitHub's trigger matches. The runner's own runs are the
@@ -88,6 +136,10 @@ export const atomaRunWatch = new Workflow("atomaton-run-watch", {
   new DefinedJob("watch", {
     "runs-on": "ubuntu-latest",
     "timeout-minutes": SCRIPT_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES,
+    // The completion half only. On a schedule there is no watched run — no title, no id, no
+    // conclusion — and the reconciliation below would read every one of them as empty; the
+    // sweep job is what a schedule runs instead.
+    if: JobCondition.of("github.event_name == 'workflow_run'"),
   }, [
     // The DEFAULT branch head, which is what `github.sha` is on a `workflow_run`
     // event — not the triggering run's head commit, whatever a first reading of
@@ -128,4 +180,34 @@ export const atomaRunWatch = new Workflow("atomaton-run-watch", {
       })}\n`,
     }),
   ]),
+).addJob(
+  // The scheduled half: the same question, asked of every node that could still be locked,
+  // without waiting for an event that never comes. See `lib/stale-sweep.ts` for what it does
+  // and `domain/work/stale-lock.ts` for the one judgement it shares with the guard.
+  new DefinedJob("sweep", {
+    "runs-on": "ubuntu-latest",
+    "timeout-minutes": SWEEP_JOB_TIMEOUT_MINUTES,
+    // The scheduled half only. A `workflow_run` event has no lock to sweep — the watch above
+    // reconciles that run by its own id — and running both would read every labelled node
+    // twice for one completion.
+    if: JobCondition.of("github.event_name == 'schedule'"),
+  }, [
+    // The DEFAULT branch head, which is what `github.sha` is on a schedule — the last
+    // committed release of this machinery, whose tag vocabulary the sweep has to read.
+    new ActionsCheckoutV4({}),
+    new SetupBunAction({ name: "Setup Bun" }),
+    new TypedOutputsStep({
+      name: "Sweep the stale locks",
+      shell: "bash",
+      env: {
+        GH_TOKEN: "${{ github.token }}",
+        GITHUB_REPOSITORY: "${{ github.repository }}",
+        GITHUB_RUN_ID: "${{ github.run_id }}",
+      },
+      // No arguments: the script reads the repository and this run's id from the
+      // environment, which is where the run itself put them. A value spliced onto the
+      // command line here would be the same value typed twice.
+      run: `${scriptCommandWithArgs(sweepStaleLocksRef, {})}\n`,
+    }),
+  ]),
